contract: A probe REPORTS. A session CLEARS the row. Nothing here writes verified_at, observation, or removes a row.

results.detail: Neither half is reachable from a scheduled probe. (a) needs /api/bot/logs?level=error, which is not under /api/diag/* and so is not served by the diag bearer this runner holds; (b) needs cancel-ib-order EXERCISED against the real gateway, which is an action, not an observation — a probe that triggered it would be making a Tier-2 mutation on a schedule.

The observable is a HUMAN-shaped event — an uncontaminated session reporting on a due item and citing the brief as where it saw it. No machine can witness that, and a probe that claimed to would be asserting an observation nobody made.

PROBE-ABLE ONCE ARMED, NOT BEFORE. The sweep ships at `annotate` with an empty allowlist, so no soak row can carry an `apply`d classification yet; a probe now would return a permanent, meaningless fail. Attach one against /api/diag/log_file?name=protection_reassert_soak (or the stray-group soak) in the same change that arms PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS.

The trainer VM has NO diag HTTP surface (relay-only, per CLAUDE.md), so this runner cannot read the capture's freshness at all. Worse, the row's own clause (a) demands the alarm be SHOWN firing against PLANTED staleness — a probe of the data's freshness would test the data, not the alarm, which is the semantic substitution the row is written to prevent.

Half (a) reads /api/bot/config, not /api/diag/*, so the diag bearer does not serve it. Half (b) needs a closed trade OPENED AFTER a named deploy sha, read against BROKER TRUTH — a journal+venue join no single soak log carries. A probe covering only (a) would pass while the row's whole point is (b).

results.checks: A pairs_soak `open` row exists in which at least one leg was placed carrying a hedge `position_idx` (1 or 2), and at least one leg reports a concurrent non-pairs `directional_open: present` — the netting collision this row exists to observe.
results.is_not: ⚠️ The `[]` fan-out is ANY-of, so the two leg conditions need not hold on the SAME leg — a pass does not establish clause (1) 'BOTH legs', and it checks clause (2) 'no half_open and no stranded leg' not at all. It is a strictly WEAKER predicate than `clears_when` by construction: treat a pass as 'go read this row', never as the criterion met. `position_idx` is also what we SENT, not a venue read-back — cross-check /api/diag/bybit_open_orders.

A FAIL over a non-zero denominator is the expected state of this row (armed, never capped); a fail over ZERO rows means the log read empty and nothing was established.

The observable is in the research CORPUS, read via `research_disposition.py --report`, not in a diag soak log. A probe is genuinely buildable here and is the obvious next one to add — it is absent because it needs the corpus reader wired as a probe, not because the condition is unobservable.

The observable is inside one GPU-routed RUN's own output, and the row explicitly refuses a dry run as evidence. A scheduled probe cannot produce that without FIRING a GPU job, which spends real budget — an action, not an observation.

Both halves live in a CI job LOG (`session-brief: verdict=inherited`, `stale-branch refresh -> …`), reachable only through the GitHub Actions API, which this runner's diag bearer does not cover. Buildable against the Actions API later; deliberately not faked against a local re-run, which the row already rules out as synthetic.
